Patch 0.41.0.28 (every wound answers with a relic)

  • Every combat outcome now leaves an intentional mark: Fighter, Rogue, Wizard, Cleric, hostile, and reflected hits each receive a compact code-generated dark-fantasy reaction instead of relying on floating numbers alone.
  • Afflictions speak their own language: bleed drips through a blood-tithe seal and poison blooms from a venom censer, keeping repeated damage readable without pretending it was another direct strike.
  • Every realm hazard wounds differently: lava, gravewind sandstorm, lightning, and wind damage use distinct cinder, grit, storm-brand, and gale-shear reactions derived from the exact authoritative hazard kind.
  • Recovery is no longer one anonymous green flash: Cleric healing, recurring restoration, lifesteal, and self-restoration now gather through separate mercy, rosary, sanguine, and pale-heart relics.
  • Damage and healing carry server truth: authoritative payloads now include semantic kind and instance identity across direct abilities, projectiles, zones, ailments, reflection, kill effects, and restoration.
  • Dungeon combat stays inside its instance: damage and healing broadcasts are routed by instance, while open-world hazard messages retain their shared overworld behavior.
  • Existing combat cues remain intact: floating numbers and involvement audio still report magnitude and urgency; the new victim-side relics complement cast and projectile art without replacing or duplicating it.
  • Busy fights stay clean: reactions are proximity-filtered and throttled per target and effect kind, so rapid ticks cannot bury actors while simultaneous bleed, poison, and direct damage remain distinguishable.
  • High and Low quality preserve the same identity: both tiers keep the core wound seal and witness halo, while Low removes only optional shards; cached immutable geometry and materials keep concurrent effects independent and cheap.
  • The browser audit now witnesses consequence and recovery: dedicated damage and restoration galleries verify all 16 identities for visible finite geometry, unique motifs, shared-cache safety, and complete cleanup.
  • Combat balance is unchanged: damage, healing, tick timing, cooldowns, resource costs, target rules, and authoritative ability footprints remain exactly where gameplay logic placed them.
  • Clients cross a clean threshold: the built-in asset generation advances to 2026-09-03-28.

Patch 0.41.0.27 (every projectile lands with consequence)

  • Every collision-capable projectile and trap now leaves its own mark: Fireball, Arcane Missile, Dragonfire Lance, Dagger, Flame Tornado, Meteor, Phantom Arrow, Tripwire, Explosive Trap, and Snare Trap each resolve through an intentional code-generated dark-fantasy impact instead of a shared flash.
  • Impact timing now belongs to the server: multiplayer clients present collisions only from a new authoritative impact event, removing the duplicate bursts, early removals, and visual disagreement caused by client-side collision guesses.
  • Area impacts show their real reach: Fireball draws its ten-unit blast, Explosive Trap draws its six-unit detonation, and every Meteor rune draws the exact landing radius supplied by authoritative combat logic.
  • Boundaries stay honest while the magic moves: each area fill and outer edge remains fixed at gameplay size while crowns, seals, hearts, shards, and binding lines animate inside it; Low quality keeps the same combat footprint.
  • Piercing and bouncing attacks acknowledge every real victim: Dagger, Dragonfire Lance, and Flame Tornado can present each server-confirmed target impact without collapsing later contacts into the first hit.
  • Expired projectiles no longer pretend they struck something: ordinary lifetime cleanup is silent, while Meteor retains a deduplicated packet-loss fallback so a real landing cannot disappear or play twice.
  • Offline combat closes its old collision holes: Phantom Arrow and all three Rogue trap families now use the same typed impact route, and local Fireball, Explosive Trap, and Meteor splash checks use their authoritative footprints.
  • Dungeon and overworld traffic stays in its lane: impact events are filtered by instance and distant overworld events are ignored unless their source or projectile is relevant to the local client.
  • Impact art is fast and independently disposable: immutable geometry and materials are cached, every effect owns its transform and teardown, and removing one impact cannot invalidate another still on screen.
  • The browser audit watches every collision family: dedicated direct-hit and area galleries verify all ten types for unique identity, visible finite geometry, and exact AOE boundaries, while unit and server coverage prove High/Low construction, cleanup, payload truth, and duplicate suppression.
  • Combat balance is unchanged: damage, cooldowns, resource costs, target rules, and server-owned radii remain intact; stale offline splash checks and visuals were aligned to those existing authoritative values.
  • Clients cross a clean threshold: the built-in asset generation advances to 2026-09-03-27.

Patch 0.41.0.26 (every ability cast becomes a rite)

  • All 52 selectable abilities now cast with an intentional identity: every Fighter, Rogue, Wizard, and Cleric presentation leaves the generic transient-effect palette for a named code-generated dark-fantasy rite.
  • Class fantasy carries through the full cast: Fighter abilities use siege wakes, war-oaths, bulwarks, and headsman wheels; Rogue abilities use blackglass blades, execution seals, venom sacraments, and eclipse shrouds.
  • Wizard and Cleric magic no longer share anonymous shapes: extinction clocks, furnace lenses, void astrolabes, mercy fonts, oath chapels, rescue wings, and last-bell decrees give each spell a distinct silhouette and palette.
  • Shield Slam finally shows its whole hit area: the cast now draws the authoritative four-unit, ninety-degree cone in addition to its target impact instead of pretending a point flash is the entire attack.
  • Every authoritative area remains exact: circular and conical gameplay boundaries carry the same radius and arc used by combat logic, stay fixed while interior relics animate, and retain that truth on Low graphics.
  • Frost Nova keeps its own winter language: the compatibility ability resolves through Flame Whip's canonical gameplay route while presenting an eight-unit rimeglass nova and winter-chain seal rather than fire.
  • Replicated casts preserve semantic identity: every remote layer now enters the same production dispatcher with canonical ability, requested alias, direction, layer index, radius, and arc instead of dropping back to anonymous point effects.
  • Generic actor wrappers no longer erase class art: remote visual resolution prefers the entity's declared mesh/class type, and the modern dispatcher no longer depends on an obsolete per-entity fallback method.
  • Cast resources are shared without shared state: immutable geometry and materials are cached by ability while each local or remote cast owns its transforms and teardown cannot invalidate a surviving peer.
  • The browser audit now checks what the player actually sees: all 112 base/rune presentations are verified in High and Low hardware Chrome for layer count, canonical/requested identity, unique motif, visible geometry, finite transforms, and exact boundaries.
  • Combat balance is unchanged: damage, cooldowns, mana, targeting, server authority, and existing radius values remain on their established paths; this patch makes their presentation truthful and distinctive.
  • Clients cross a clean threshold: the built-in asset generation advances to 2026-09-03-26.

Patch 0.41.0.25 (every condition bears its own relic)

  • All 23 attached conditions now have an intentional silhouette: every replicated buff and debuff, plus the offline freeze compatibility state, leaves the shared ring-and-orb templates for a named code-native relic construction.
  • Fighter vows read as iron and consequence: Iron Fortress forms a riveted bastion cage, Guardian Roar marches oath shields, Berserker Edge raises hooked bloodsteel, and Last Stand carries a broken final crown.
  • Rogue states stay sharp and secretive: Serrated Edges becomes a blackglass saw-vow, Poison Coating carries fangs and vials, and Stealth closes an eclipse shroud around its owner.
  • Wizard control has a mechanical language: Spell Focus turns through a violet astrolabe lens, Arcane Shield closes a sixfold sapphire shell, and Time Warp runs a gilded chronicle with contrary hands.
  • Cleric blessings become visible covenants: Guardian Embrace, Resolve, Divine Intervention, and Zeal now use reliquary arms, pilgrim shields, rescue wings, and ember-gold sunblades instead of recolored generic pieces.
  • Control and affliction states are readable at a glance: marks, stun, root, slow, freeze, bleed, and poison receive distinct execution, broken-vow, concussion, grave-root, winter-chain, rimeglass, blood-tithe, and venom-censer motifs.
  • Local and replicated characters use the same status factory: authoritative snapshot reconstruction, expiry, death cleanup, scene restoration, and quality changes all retain one semantic visual route.
  • Status resources are pooled safely: immutable geometry and materials are generated once and shared while every owner keeps an independent pose; removing one condition never disposes resources used by another actor.
  • Freeze can no longer recolor unrelated characters: the dormant legacy tint mutated pooled actor materials, so the new per-owner frost prison now owns freeze readability without cross-instance contamination.
  • Deterministic evidence starts clean every time: the gallery now resets every buff, debuff, multiplier, and movement-control timer before presenting the next state.
  • Hardware Chrome audits every condition twice: all 23 statuses are exercised on local High-quality actors and replicated Low-quality actors with unique metadata, finite transforms, single-effect ownership, representative plates, and zero-effect cleanup.
  • Clients cross a clean threshold: the built-in asset generation advances to 2026-09-03-25.

Patch 0.41.0.24 (the ground remembers every spell)

  • The last generic local area meshes are gone: Burning Ground, offline Inferno Cataclysm, Gravity Well, and the Smoke Bomb gallery field now use explicit multi-part code-native constructions instead of a tinted cylinder, sphere, or ring.
  • Each field has its own ritual language: fire scars carry cinder script and crown flames, Gravity Well becomes a void astrolabe prison, and Smoke Bomb forms a blackglass concealment shroud with translucent low-poly wisps.
  • Gravity Well's old radius drift is fixed: the offline fallback and visual gallery now use the server's authoritative eight-unit base radius and twelve-unit Expanded radius instead of the stale six- and five-unit values.
  • Inferno stays exact in every mode: its local fallback resolves the same twelve-unit registry boundary used by the replicated server zone, while Burning Ground retains its intended 3.5-unit damage radius.
  • Smoke Bomb's evidence uses its real five-unit reach: the procedural gallery field no longer displays the old four-unit placeholder.
  • Boundaries do not breathe or lie: only interior brands, captured shards, and wisps animate; the outer gameplay edge remains fixed at the declared radius for the full field lifetime.
  • Low graphics remains readable: reduced-quality fields remove ornaments while preserving the identical field fill, boundary, identity, and collision metadata.
  • Field instances reuse immutable geometry and materials: expiration, chunk removal, and gallery cleanup detach each root without destroying resources still used by another active field.
  • The gallery no longer doubles target-anchored world effects: local and replicated actors share one ground object, eliminating overlap flicker and false brightness in deterministic evidence.
  • One-shot animation QA is deterministic: the gallery records that Attack actually started even when a very short clip has legitimately returned to Idle before the browser samples it.
  • Hardware Chrome now proves both Gravity Well sizes and Smoke Bomb: isolated effect plates, finite-transform checks, the 112-variant ability matrix, every actor state, and cleanup all pass together.
  • Clients cross a clean threshold: the built-in asset generation advances to 2026-09-03-24.

Patch 0.41.0.23 (spells carry their own relics)

  • Projectiles are no longer colored primitives: Fireball, Arcane Missile, Dragonfire Lance, Dagger, Flame Tornado, Meteor, and Phantom Arrow now travel as distinct multi-part dark-fantasy relics.
  • Every moving spell has a readable construction: ember cages, violet reliquary seals, dragon barbs, blacksteel guards, cinder helices, fault-crowned extinction stone, and void feathers separate the seven silhouettes at the gameplay camera.
  • Rogue traps now say what they do: Tripwire uses posts and three tension lines, Explosive Trap forms a cinder-tooth mine, and Snare Trap closes around paired venom jaws.
  • Persistent zones become ritual spaces: Inferno Cataclysm carries animated magma faults and cinders, Consecrated Ground uses reliquary rays and oath pearls, and the compatibility zone has its own crossed old-ward seal.
  • Zone edges remain combat truth: outer boundaries never pulse beyond their hit area, and server-encoded scale makes the persistent Inferno seal show its complete 12-unit radius rather than the old five-unit disc.
  • Offline and online Tripwire agree: the local trigger and visible tension field now use the server's 1.5-unit radius.
  • Reconnects reconstruct the same art: every authoritative projectile subtype routes through the same synchronous code-native factory for the caster, observers, and resumed state.
  • Effects reuse their bones: geometry and materials are cached across instances while every projectile, trap, and zone keeps independent motion and can be detached without destroying shared resources.
  • The audit fails on an unnamed projectile: tests derive all 12 server-created subtypes from the Go ability handlers and require an explicit production visual; the documented legacy zone is the only compatibility alias.
  • Hardware evidence now includes three dedicated effect plates: all seven projectiles, all three traps, and all three zones render with finite transforms alongside the full ability and cleanup matrix.
  • Clients cross a clean threshold: the built-in asset generation advances to 2026-09-03-23.

Patch 0.41.0.22 (no silhouette left unnamed)

  • The last generic overworld actors have found their forms: all ten Cinder Wastes and Stormcrown Reach enemies leave the shared shape-and-scale builder for distinct regional rigs.
  • Cinder now has a complete hostile procession: the floating Ash-Dune Djinn, fault-plated Magma Golem, ribbed Scorched Wraith, low quadruped Infernal Behemoth, and broad-winged Phoenix Sentinel each read as a different threat.
  • Stormcrown owns more than one kind of storm: the masked Gale-Talon Harpy, Captive-Cloud Elemental, Conductor Roc, Thunder-Cairn Giant, and Hollow-Cyclone Avatar carry separate proportions, weapons, and motion.
  • The sky creatures finally fly as silhouettes: phoenix and roc bodies use broad articulated feather fans, long tails, breast keels, crowned heads, talons, and orbiting realm energy instead of enlarged primitive birds.
  • The behemoth is no longer another tall humanoid: a wide four-legged kiln beast with a horned bull skull, cloven hooves, tusks, furnace ribs, and caldera spine occupies the Cinder herd role.
  • Every remaining elemental has a readable heart: magma faults, captive cloud cairns, crossed pressure rings, storm conductors, and hollow cyclone blades make faction and attack language visible at the gameplay camera.
  • Movement remains authoritative: all ten retain their original AI, spawn identity, 1.25-unit combat radius, and replicated idle, walk, run, attack, and death state names.
  • Large wings and floating rings do not change hits: full visible selection bounds are declared separately from combat radii and every reused mesh owns one current interaction box.
  • The generic production actor registry is now empty: every current combat actor type has explicit synchronous factory, catalog, animation-manifest, pool, and gallery coverage with no model-loader request.
  • Hardware Chrome sees the entire bestiary: local and replicated copies of all 47 actor archetypes render through every relevant state at High and Low quality with finite transforms.
  • Clients cross a clean threshold: the built-in asset generation advances to 2026-09-03-22.

Patch 0.41.0.21 (the drowned crown rises)

  • The Drowned Sanctum has raised its five sovereign horrors: every Abyssal Well boss leaves the shared shape catalog for a purpose-built basalt, drowned iron, coral, pearl, and black-tide rig.
  • Tiderend coils through a broken tide: twelve articulated body scales, broad coral fins, maw tendrils, pearl eyes, depth-orbit stones, and a reef crown make the first encounter visibly serpentine.
  • The Drowned Choir is many voices but one encounter: three elevated cantor masks, individual coral crowns, a ribcage harp, voice pearls, and a drowned chime preserve one authoritative boss while making its collective form unmistakable.
  • The Goliath carries a graveyard on its back: sixteen sunken cairn slabs, oversized anchor fists, soul stones, a burial crown, chain, and grave anchor give the brute a low, crushing silhouette.
  • The Maelstrom Warden locks the chamber: layered tide rings, a shell mantle, orbiting pearls, and a moon-anchor polearm turn the fourth guardian into a moving ritual bulwark.
  • Thalorath finally sits beneath all tides: sixteen throne tentacles, nine black-tide rings, thirteen coral crown spires, sixteen throne pearls, and a luminous deep trident frame the final king.
  • Every drowned body speaks the network's language: generated idle, walk, run, attack, and stable death performances retain the existing replicated animation-state contract.
  • Encounter scale and combat truth remain separate: each visible body declares exact selection bounds while all five preserve the unchanged 1.25-unit server-authoritative combat radius and one actor-owned interaction hitbox.
  • Idle bosses no longer drown in a missing reference: all five Abyssal Well actors now import the Three.js vector used by their roaming path, with a direct regression covering the timer-triggered branch.
  • No abyssal form hides behind a loader: direct synchronous factory routing, cached immutable geometry and materials, independent poses, pool safety, finite-transform checks, and High/Low hardware galleries cover the complete family.
  • Clients cross a clean threshold: the built-in asset generation advances to 2026-09-03-21.

Patch 0.41.0.20 (the sky remembers its teeth)

  • The Shattered Aerie has claimed its five wardens: every Tempest Spire boss leaves the generic shape catalog for an individually generated slate, silver, violet, and captive-storm rig.
  • Windshear is a pressure front given a blade: floating gale tatters, six vacuum rings, fourteen razor vanes, orbiting pressure shards, and a white-sky scythe form a narrow cutting silhouette.
  • Voltara and Zephyros speak through one storm: the Stormcallers remain one authoritative encounter actor while two distinct masked oracles, split halos, convergence sparks, and a forked staff make the duo visible.
  • The Roc Matriarch owns the horizon: a true airborne body carries twenty-two long storm feathers, nine tail plumes, silver talons, a crowned head, and a lightning-lit breast keel.
  • Kaelix has become the conductor throne: captive lightning, ten silver rods, a nine-spire storm-bell crown, and a thunder maul give the fourth encounter giant weight and ritual purpose.
  • Zephyrion stands inside the Eternal Gale: nine crossed vortex rings, sixteen horizon blades, thirteen crown spires, orbiting eye shards, and a sky scepter surround the final sovereign.
  • Flight, drift, stride, strike, and collapse remain network-readable: every boss owns generated idle, walk, run, attack, and stable death performances under the existing replicated state names.
  • The wide wings do not widen the rules: each visible form has a declared selection volume while every boss keeps the unchanged 1.25-unit server-authoritative combat radius.
  • No storm is a hidden fallback: all five types route directly through synchronous factories, share cached immutable resources, retain actor-owned poses, and no longer appear in the generic enemy-shape catalog.
  • The entire procession faces inspection: unit and hardware-Chrome coverage checks every state, High and Low presentation, grounding, bounds, cache reuse, pooling, loader bypass, and finite transforms.
  • Clients cross a clean threshold: the built-in asset generation advances to 2026-09-03-20.

Patch 0.41.0.19 (five hearts beneath the anvil)

  • The Furnace Below has found its monsters: all five Molten Core bosses leave the generic scaled-shape system for individually built, code-generated encounter rigs.
  • Cindermaw runs like the beast it is: a true four-legged cinder-hound carries a rib kiln, articulated fire maw, brass fangs, caldera spines, horns, claws, and a long black-iron chain tail.
  • The Scorched Twins share one terrible oath: two divided masked upper bodies rise from one authoritative covenant brand, wielding a split ember-and-white-fire glaive without pretending two server actors exist.
  • Pyrax brings the forge into battle: the Forgemaster bears a caged white-hot heart, chain apron, six burning chimneys, and a massive oath-anvil hammer.
  • The Guardian is a wall of black glass: an armored sealed core, jagged obsidian crest, branded octagonal bulwark, and monolithic collapse make the fourth boss readable before it strikes.
  • Infernax finally wears the Ashen Throne: an eleven-spire crown, horned furnace mask, throne mantle, nine orbiting censers, and caldera scepter give the final boss a silhouette worthy of the last chamber.
  • Every boss moves with its own weight: generated idle, walk, run, attack, and stable death performances cover quadruped and biped bodies while preserving the existing replicated animation-state contract.
  • Large bodies no longer enlarge the rules: full visible silhouettes receive exact declared selection bounds, while the unchanged 1.25-unit authoritative combat radius remains independent for every encounter.
  • No old model is hiding underneath: each Molten boss routes synchronously through its dedicated factory, bypasses authored loading and the generic enemy-shape catalog, reuses immutable render resources, and keeps actor poses independent.
  • The whole furnace procession is inspectable: unit and hardware-Chrome coverage exercises every boss, every state, both quality tiers, cache stability, pooling, bounds, and non-finite transform protection.
  • Clients cross a clean threshold: the built-in asset generation advances to 2026-09-03-19.
